title: Comets, monsters and the Apocalypse: Christie's to offer The Book of Miracles
summary: Comets, monsters, celestial battles and visions of the Apocalypse come to life in The Book of Miracles (estimate: £700,000-1,000,000) also known as the Augsburger Wunderzeichenbuch, an exceptional illustrated manuscript created in Augsburg around 1552. Comprising 167 vividly painted miniatures, the work is one of the most remarkable surviving picture chronicles of the 16th century. It will lead Christie's Valuable Books & Manuscripts sale in London on 10 December 2026, part of the house's Classic Week programme, and is being offered from An Alchemy of Ideas: Works from the Mickey Cartin Collection. Beginning with the Creation and moving chronologically through biblical events, ancient and medieval history, contemporary happenings and ultimately the Apocalypse, The Book of Miracles offers a vivid visual history of a world in which extraordinary phenomena were understood as signs carrying meaning for humanity. title: University Archives December auction features rare Edgar Allan Poe receipt and first edition Harry Potter
summary: A 1st edition 1st printing hardcover copy of J.K. Rowling’s Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone from 1997; a receipt note signed by Edgar Allan Poe, likely related to his poem The Raven; and a color engraving of Abraham Lincoln reading a draft of the Emancipation Proclamation, accompanied by his signature and those of seven of his cabinet members are a few of the historical items up for bid in University Archives’ online-only Rare Autographs, Manuscripts, Books & Photographs auction set for December 2nd. The auction, starting at 10am ET, is filled with important and significant items in a variety of categories. The entire catalog – 476 lots – is up for viewing and bidding now on the University Archives website – www.UniversityArchives.com – as well as the platforms Invaluable.com, LiveAuctioneers.com and Auctionzip.com. title: The Met's first exhibition of Japanese photography in more than three decades explores a nation in transition
summary: The Metropolitan Museum of Art presents A Long Shadow: Postwar Japan Through the Lens, an exhibition that examines how photographers in Japan recorded, questioned, and helped reshape a society in transition in the decades after World War II. On view November 12, 2026, through May 2, 2027, the exhibition draws on the Museum's collection to bring together works from an intergenerational group of 15 artists, from Tōmatsu Shōmei (Aichi, Nagoya 1930–2012 Naha, Okinawa), a pioneer of postwar Japanese photography, to contemporary Okinawan filmmaker Yamashiro Chikako (born Okinawa, 1976). Also featured are photographs and books by Ishiuchi Miyako (born Gunma, 1947), Ishikawa Mao (born Okinawa, 1953), Tokiwa Toyoko (Yokohama, Kanagawa 1928–2019), and Heshiki Kenshichi (Nakijin, Okinawa 1948–2009), among others. title: Museo Nacional del Prado explores Spanish art's influence on poet Rainer Maria Rilke
summary: To mark the centenary of the death of Rainer Maria Rilke (Prague, 1875-Montreux, 1926), the Museo Nacional del Prado, in collaboration with the City Council of Madrid and the Community of Madrid, is presenting an exhibition that analyses the influence of Spanish art and culture on the intellectual and literary trajectory of one of the great European poets of the 20th century. The exhibition explores Rilke's relationship with Spanish art, from his early writings on Velázquez and Murillo to his interest in El Greco, Goya, Ignacio Zuloaga, Pablo Picasso and María Blanchard. Through paintings, drawings, historical photographs, publications, manuscripts and correspondence, it reveals how artistic contemplation became an essential source of knowledge and creation for the poet. title: Sotheby's reveals all of the art heading to Abu Dhabi auction this December
summary: Next month, Sotheby's is set to stage Abu Dhabi's first-ever international art auction. Titled 'Breaking Ground', the sale is named in homage to the pioneering ethos of Abu Dhabi, where one of the most impressive cultural districts in the world has been forged from the ground up. Today, the entire offering of some fifty lots is revealed, as the auction catalogue goes live, with works by the likes of Pablo Picasso, Claude Monet, Andy Warhol, Roy Lichtenstein and Yayoi Kusama sitting alongside Middle Eastern pioneers including Mohamed Ahmed Ibrahim, Hassan Sharif, Monir Farmanfarmaian, Fahrelnissa Zeid and Huguette Caland. The auction will take place in the heart of Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi's world-class cultural destination, at the new Saadiyat Grove Experience Center - a stone's throw away from the Louvre Abu Dhabi and the Guggenheim Abu Dhabi. title: From overlooked art to American masterpieces: Museum founder releases new memoir
summary: The National Museum of American Illustration announced the official release of Reframed: How Seeing Value in Overlooked Art Changed My Life , the highly anticipated memoir of its founder and director, Judy Goffman Cutler. Now available for purchase on Amazon, the richly illustrated book chronicles an extraordinary fifty-year journey of discovery, determination, and a lifelong mission to rescue and revive appreciation for America's greatest illustrators. At 84, Judy reflects on an unlikely career that began with a simple appreciation for beautiful paintings and grew into a pioneering effort to transform the way the art world views American illustration. title: Margot Heller to step down as Director of the South London Gallery in spring 2027
summary: Margot Heller, the long-standing Director of the South London Gallery (SLG), has announced that she will step down in spring 2027 to embark on a new chapter in her career as an independent curator and advisor. Margot Heller said: “The South London Gallery has been a huge part of my life and I believe passionately in its importance. After 25 years at the helm, I feel it’s time for new adventures in my career. It has been a privilege to lead the physical and organisational expansion of the SLG over the years, and to work with an exceptional staff team and brilliant board of trustees. I have relished programming and curating countless exhibitions in the beautiful gallery spaces. Most of all, I have been honoured to work with a huge number of exceptional artists on some amazing projects. title: Gerda Ridler concludes five transformative years at Austria's Landesgalerie Niederösterreich
summary: When Gerda Ridler steps down as artistic director of the Landesgalerie Niederösterreich in December 2026, she will leave behind a museum whose identity has become closely associated with her commitment to women artists, ambitious contemporary installations, and the rich cultural heritage of Lower Austria. Over the course of five years, Ridler oversaw 26 exhibitions, introduced important changes to the museum's exhibition spaces, and helped establish the institution as a place where regional artistic traditions could engage in meaningful dialogue with contemporary practices from around the world. Perhaps the clearest expression of her priorities can be found in one striking figure: 16 of those 26 exhibitions were devoted to the work of women artists. For Ridler, this was not simply a question of achieving greater representation. title: A monumental Pskov icon and rediscovered Romanov jewel lead Heritage's Dec. 8 Russian Works of Art auction
summary: A monumental 16th-century icon preserved in one American family for nearly a century, a rare military decoration from the age of Napoleon and a jeweled crown brooch newly connected to a Romanov grand duchess headline Heritage’s Dec. 8 Russian Works of Art Signature® Auction. The auction brings together exceptional objects of devotion, Imperial porcelain and historic jewelry and paintings, including a collection descending directly from the family of artist Boris Chaliapin. “These are works with remarkable stories, and the research behind this auction has brought several of those stories back into focus,” says Nick Nicholson, Heritage’s Deputy Chairman of Decorative Arts and Director of Russian Works of Art. “From an extraordinary early icon to a small jewel whose Imperial history had been forgotten, the sale offers collectors the opportunity to discover something consequential.”

title: MAXXI Rome presents major retrospective on American artist Gordon Matta-Clark
summary: MAXXI, the National Museum of 21st Century Arts, presents Gordon Matta-Clark. Not the Work... The Worker, an exhibition curated by Jessamyn Fiore and Francesco Stocchi, dedicated to one of the most innovative figures on the international art scene of the 1970s. Through sculptures, photographs, films, and spatial interventions, the exhibition explores the artistic practice of the American artist (New York, 1943–1978), who transformed architecture into a field of artistic, political, and social experimentation. Particular attention is given to his experiences in Italy, which played a decisive role in the evolution of his artistic language. The exhibition was also developed in consultation with an international scientific committee of artists, architects, and scholars, comprising Laurie Anderson, Martien De Vletter, Elizabeth Diller, Julien Fronsacq, Lorenzo Fusi, Francesco Garutti, Alfredo Jaar, Joan Jonas, Noah Khoshbin, Sylvia Lavin, Camila Mancilla Vera, Azikiwe Mohammed, and Sok

title: The Museum of Contemporary Art Australia appoints Sophie O'Brien as Senior Curator, Exhibitions
summary: The Museum of Contemporary Art Australia (MCA Australia) is delighted to announce a major addition to its senior curatorial team with the appointment of Sophie O'Brien as Senior Curator, Exhibitions. Sophie O'Brien is an experienced and respected curator and writer, who has forged a reputation for commissioning ambitious, large-scale projects and programming across disciplines, both nationally and internationally over her 25-year career. Sophie joins the MCA from Bundanon, where, as Head of Curatorial & Learning, she led the development and delivery of an expanded artistic program for the organisation's new Art Museum. title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art announces major collaboration agreement with the Shanghai museum
summary: On November 16, The Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Shanghai Museum signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) formalizing a shared commitment to advancing the presentation and study of art and heritage, and fostering deeper collaboration between the two institutions, including exhibitions, research initiatives, and curatorial exchange. The MOU was signed at the Shanghai Museum People's Square by Max Hollein, The Met's Director and CEO, and Chu Xiaobo, Director of the Shanghai Museum. "Our collaboration with the Shanghai Museum is rooted in a shared belief in the power of art to foster understanding between cultures," said Max Hollein, The Met's Director and CEO. title: Esther Schipper announces representation of Madrid-based sculptor Teresa Solar Abboud
summary: Esther Schipper announced the representation of Teresa Solar Abboud. Teresa Solar Abboud was born in 1985 in Madrid. The artist holds a BFA from Universidad Complutense de Madrid and graduated with an MA in Cultural Studies from Universidad Europea de Madrid in 2009. She currently lives and works in Madrid. Teresa Solar Abboud has established a distinctive position in contemporary sculpture. Her works let viewers enter a fantastic world of shifting relationships between forms, colors and bodies. Vaguely familiar shapes appear suspended in their surroundings, without reference to scale, human or otherwise. A gentle curve of one of her sculptures, for example, can hold echoes of single-cell lifeforms, tiny sea creatures, marine animals, the fin of a whale, a human limb and mechanical tools. title: Legendary Silver Dollar, a secret mint rarity, to bring $2M+
summary: The Book of Ecclesiastes famously said “there is nothing new under the sun.” The French have a famous axiom that translates to “the more things change, the more they stay the same.” In 1885, a powerful political appointee named A. Loudon Snowden retired, ending a decades-long career at the United States Mint in Philadelphia that saw him relentlessly use his position for personal gain. His career began when his uncle — the former speaker of the Pennsylvania State House and Treasurer of Pennsylvania — gave him a job at age 22, fresh out of college. Over the decades that followed, Snowden oversaw the off-the-books production of thousands of delicacies for coin collectors, enriching himself and others in the process. title: Newly discovered 160-year-old painting by Frances Anne Hopkins makes auction debut
summary: A collection of 75 rare, important and museum-quality artworks are headed to auction on Wednesday, November 25 with Cowley Abbott?s Fall Live Auction: Select Masterworks of Canadian and International Art. The sale is a survey of Canada?s most celebrated artists ? including Emily Carr, Lawren Harris and other members of the Group of Seven, Maurice Cullen, Norval Morrisseau, William Kurelek, Ivan Eyre, and Rita Letendre ? presenting a time capsule of more than two centuries of Canadian art history captured in precise brush strokes and vibrant detail. title: Cardi Gallery Milan presents solo survey of post-war master Agostino Bonalumi
summary: Cardi Gallery Milan is presenting a solo exhibition dedicated to the work of Agostino Bonalumi, one of the defining figures of post-war Italian art. Organised in collaboration with Archivio Bonalumi, Agostino Bonalumi. Tertium non datur – Il colore che manca brings together over twenty monochromatic works from across the artist's experimental career, offering a survey of his most significant series from 1964 to 2013, the year of his passing. The title of the exhibition, a Latin phrase which refers to the law of excluded middle ('no third is given'), takes a cue from the rigorous chromatic, formal and material investigations that formed the essence of Bonalumi's art. title: Saint-Gaudens's 'Victory' soars to $2 million as Rockwell shines in Heritage's record-breaking American Art auction
summary: A rare gilded bronze of Augustus Saint-Gaudens’s Victory realized $2 million at Heritage Auctions Nov. 13, achieving the second-highest auction price for a work by the artist. The winged figure, whose monumental counterpart strides before General William Tecumseh Sherman at the southeastern entrance to Central Park, helped propel Heritage’s American Art Signature® Auction to $12.65 million — the second-highest total for an American Art auction in Heritage’s history. Behind Victory’s sweeping wings and forward momentum is Hettie Anderson, the Black model whose poise and physical discipline helped Saint-Gaudens give an American ideal human form. title: Armenian Museum of America begins major exterior renovation to transform museum's presence
summary: The Armenian Museum of America is entering an exciting new chapter as it begins major improvements to the exterior of its historic building in Greater Boston. Contracts for the first phase of exterior façade work were signed in October, with construction beginning this fall. The project represents an important investment in the Museum’s future, preserving and enhancing its historic building while creating a more welcoming and visually compelling presence for visitors, neighbors, and the broader community. The Museum is working with SMMA (Symmes Maini & McKee Associates), a Cambridge-based architecture and design firm, along with Alpha Weatherproofing and W.T. Kenney Painting. title: Exhibition showcases fashion and advertising photography by mid-century master William Helburn
summary: Photographer and director William Helburn straddled high fashion photography along with advertising campaigns designed to appeal to the masses, helping to define visual culture in mid-century America. Raised in New York City, Helburn learned photography when he joined the army in 1942. Following the war, he returned home with the hope of launching an aerial mapping business. A chance encounter with photographer Fernand Fonssagrives inspired him to then pursue photography, initially taking model agency test shots and studying at the workshops of legendary art director Alexey Brodovitch’s Design Laboratory. Helburn’s fellow students included Irving Penn, Richard Avedon, Robert Frank, and Diane Arbus. title: Sapieha Palace presents Nikhil Vettukattil's first institutional solo exhibition 'Years'
summary: Nikhil Vettukattil’s first institutional solo exhibition, Years (curated by Inesa Brašiškė and Povilas Gumbis), traces the final decade of the twentieth century as the threshold of our present, moving through its defining geopolitical events, contested microhistories, cultural milestones and technological breakthroughs. Conceived as a multisensory environment, it engages the various modes of representation that shape our memories and imagination of the 1990s and history more broadly. The exhibition’s conceptual starting point is Alienation (2021), a video installation featuring 560 scanned and cropped photographs from three seminal photobooks of the decade—Sebastião Salgado’s Workers: An Archaeology of the Industrial Age (1993), Michael Kenna’s The Rouge (1995), and Michael Schmidt’s U-NI-TY (1996)—alongside a video of stock

title: Fraunces Tavern Museum celebrates Martha Washington in its latest special exhibition
summary: Martha Washington – familiar to many, but few people have come to know the person behind the name. Fraunces Tavern Museum is delighted to announce our new special exhibition Martha, The First Founding Mother Revealed in the Adeline Moses Loeb Gallery. As part of the Museum's broader Path to Liberty: The Emergence of a Nation Semiquincentennial exhibition, it will bring Martha to life. The preview reception will be held on November 16, 2026, in the Kathryn and Shelby Cullom Davis Educational Center for American History adjacent to the Loeb Gallery, with an optional dinner to follow in Fraunces Tavern. The exhibition will be open to the public beginning November 17, 2026. title: Jakopič Gallery unites Hungarian photography pioneers Kertész, Moholy-Nagy, and Capa
summary: Jakopič Gallery announced an exhibition of three classics of Hungarian photography: André Kertész, László Moholy-Nagy, and Robert Capa. New Perspectives, Distinct Paths. The Hungarian Pioneers of Modern Photography brings together approximately 180 exhibition prints to explore how three independent, enduring photographic languages emerged, and how shared experiences helped shape these bodies of work to become defining chapters in the history of modern photography. The exhibition is a collaboration with the Robert Capa Contemporary Photography Center in Budapest and with the Liszt Institute in Ljubljana to mark the 10th anniversary of its founding. title: Marc Straus New York presents artist Gisela McDaniel's first gallery solo
summary: Marc Straus is presenting (Ti)p of the Spear, Gisela McDaniel's first solo exhibition with the gallery, bringing together thirteen new paintings made for her New York debut. McDaniel began much of the work on Guam, where she was the 2026 Inaugural Artist-in-Residence at the Isla Center for the Arts at the University of Guam. The series draws on oral history recordings, gifted artifacts and photographs of Indigenous CHamorus of Guåhan, nearly all of them engaged in climate work. McDaniel calls the people she paints subject collaborators. They set the pace and the content of the encounter, choose how they pose, select the photograph she works from, and are consulted as the painting proceeds; her stated aim is that they see themselves in it. title: National Gallery brings life-sized masterpiece reproductions to five UK locations
summary: The National Gallery will be partnering with Armagh City and Banbridge and Craigavon Borough Council, Greenfield Valley Museum & Heritage Park in Flintshire, Preston Park in Stockton-on-Tees, The McManus: Dundee’s Art Gallery & Museum in collaboration with Dundee City Council and Southend-on-Sea City Council for its third and final year of Art On Your Doorstep. Reproductions of masterpieces from the National Gallery will be exhibited in these locations, bringing paintings from the collection beyond Trafalgar Square. Each painting will be reproduced life-sized, in fine detail and in its frame, allowing visitors the chance to look closely and discover hidden details.
